text: Disruption of cell adhesion drives cancer dedifferentiation, invasion, and metastasis. Immunohistochemistry of desmoglein 1/2/3, desmocollin 2, integrin beta 4 (ITGB4), laminin gamma chain 2 (LAMC2), and collagen type 17 alpha 1 (COL17A1) was performed in 51 oral squamous cell carcinoma cases. In normal oral epithelium, DSG1, DSG3, DSC2, and COL17A1 localized to the plasma membrane, while ITGB4 and mature LAMC2 localized to the basement membrane. In cancer, DSG1, DSG3, DSC2, and COL17A1 decreased and internalized cytoplasmically; DSG2, ITGB4, and LAMC2 showed induced cytoplasmic expression in stroma-facing cells. Reduced DSG3 and DSC2 correlated with less differentiation, greater invasiveness, and higher nodal metastasis; lower COL17A1 and higher LAMC2 also indicated aggressive phenotype. Aberrant expression and localization of desmosomal and hemidesmosomal proteins therefore associate with aggressive clinicopathological features.
